translations.literal: if they can capture an accomplice, reward is still given according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: if they capture an accomplice, they still receive reward according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 其於事主有所損傷，及準首再犯，不在原免之例。

translations.literal: If the victim was injured, or if it is a repeat offense treated as surrender, they are not within the scope of forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Cases involving injury to the victim, or repeat offenses treated as surrender, are not eligible for forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 諸杖罪以下，府州追勘明白，即聽斷決。

translations.literal: As to all offenses of beating with the staff and below: once the prefecture or district has investigated clearly, judgment may be rendered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses punishable by the staff or less may be judged immediately once the prefecture or district has completed a clear investigation.

sentences.zh: 徒罪，總管府決配，仍申合幹上司照驗。

translations.literal: Penal servitude is decided and assigned by the circuit intendant's office, which still reports to the competent superior for verification.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude is decided and assigned by the circuit intendant's office, with report to the competent superior for verification.

sentences.zh: 流罪以上，須牒廉訪司官，審覆無冤，方得結案，依例待報。

translations.literal: Exile and above require a memorial to the Surveillance Commission official; only after review finds no injustice may the case be closed, and report is awaited according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Exile and graver penalties require referral to the Surveillance Commission; the case may close only after review finds no injustice, and final report is awaited according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 其徒伴有未獲，追會有不完者，如復審既定，贓驗明白，理無可疑，亦聽依上歸結。

translations.literal: If accomplices in penal servitude have not yet been caught, or restitution remains incomplete, yet re-review is already settled, the stolen goods verified clearly, and no doubt remains in principle, closure is still permitted according to the above.
translations.idiomatic: If accomplices remain at large or restitution is incomplete, but re-review is settled, the evidence of stolen goods is clear, and no reasonable doubt remains, the case may still be closed as above.

sentences.zh: 諸強盜持仗但傷人者，雖不得財，皆死。

translations.literal: As to all armed robbers who injure anyone: even if no property is obtained, all are put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Armed robbers who injure anyone are all put to death, even if they obtain no property.

sentences.zh: 不曾傷人，不得財，徒二年半；

translations.literal: If no one was injured and no property was obtained: penal servitude two and a half years;
translations.idiomatic: If no one was injured and no property was taken: two and a half years of penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 但得財，徒三年；

translations.literal: if property was obtained: penal servitude three years;
translations.idiomatic: if property was obtained: three years of penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 至二十貫，為首者死，余人流遠。

translations.literal: up to twenty guan, the ringleader is put to death and the rest are exiled to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: up to twenty guan, the ringleader is executed and the rest exiled afar.

sentences.zh: 不持仗傷人者，惟造意及下手者死。

translations.literal: Those who injure without bearing arms: only the instigator and the one who struck the blow are put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers who injure without bearing arms: only the instigator and the one who struck the blow are executed.

sentences.zh: 不曾傷人，不得財徒一年半，十貫以下徒二年；

translations.literal: If no one was injured and no property was obtained, penal servitude one and a half years; if under ten guan, penal servitude two years;
translations.idiomatic: If no one was injured and no property was taken, one and a half years of penal servitude; if the loot is under ten guan, two years;

sentences.zh: 每十貫加一等，至四十貫，為首者死，余人各徒三年。

translations.literal: for each ten guan increase one degree; up to forty guan, the ringleader is put to death and the rest each receive penal servitude three years.
translations.idiomatic: each additional ten guan increases the penalty one degree; at forty guan the ringleader is executed and the rest each receive three years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 若因盜而奸，同傷人之坐，其同行人止依本法，謀而未行者，於不得財罪上，各減一等坐之。

translations.literal: If during robbery there is also adultery, it is punished the same as injury; fellow participants are sentenced only under this statute; those who plotted but did not act are each reduced one degree from the penalty for obtaining no property.
translations.idiomatic: Adultery during robbery is punished as injury; accomplices are sentenced under this statute alone; plotters who did not act receive one degree less than the penalty for robbery without gain.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜始謀而未行者，笞四十七；

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves who first plot but do not act: forty-seven strokes of the bamboo;
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves who plot but do not act receive forty-seven strokes of the bamboo;

sentences.zh: 已行而不得財者，五十七；

translations.literal: if they act but obtain no property: fifty-seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: if they act but obtain no property: fifty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 得財十貫以下，六十七；

translations.literal: if property obtained is under ten guan: sixty-seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: if the loot is under ten guan: sixty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 至二十貫，七十七。

translations.literal: up to twenty guan: seventy-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: up to twenty guan: seventy-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 每二十貫加一等，一百貫，徒一年，每一百貫加一等，罪止徒三年。

translations.literal: For each twenty guan increase one degree; at one hundred guan, penal servitude one year; for each one hundred guan increase one degree; the penalty stops at penal servitude three years.
translations.idiomatic: Each additional twenty guan increases the penalty one degree; at one hundred guan the sentence is one year of penal servitude; each additional hundred guan increases it one degree, up to a maximum of three years.

sentences.zh: 諸盜庫藏錢物者，比常盜加一等，贓滿至五百貫以上者流。

translations.literal: As to all who steal money and goods from the treasury: one degree above ordinary theft; if the loot reaches five hundred guan or more, exile.
translations.idiomatic: Theft from the treasury is punished one degree above ordinary theft; loot of five hundred guan or more brings exile.

sentences.zh: 諸盜駝馬牛驢騾，一陪九。

translations.literal: As to all who steal camels, horses, cattle, donkeys, or mules: ninefold restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Those who steal camels, horses, cattle, donkeys, or mules must make ninefold restitution.

sentences.zh: 盜駱駝者，初犯為首九十七，徒二年半，為從八十七，徒二年；

translations.literal: Those who steal camels: on a first offense the ringleader receives ninety-seven strokes and penal servitude two and a half years; the follower eighty-seven strokes and penal servitude two years;
translations.idiomatic: Camel thieves on a first offense: the ringleader receives ninety-seven strokes and two and a half years of penal servitude; the follower eighty-seven strokes and two years;

sentences.zh: 再犯加等；

translations.literal: on a repeat offense increase the degree;
translations.idiomatic: on repeat offense the penalty is increased;

sentences.zh: 三犯不分首從，一百七，出軍。

translations.literal: on a third offense, without distinguishing ringleader and follower: one hundred seven strokes and banishment to military service.
translations.idiomatic: on a third offense, regardless of ringleader or follower: one hundred seven strokes and banishment to military service.

sentences.zh: 盜馬者，初犯為首八十七，徒二年，為從七十七，徒一年半；

translations.literal: Those who steal horses: on a first offense the ringleader receives eighty-seven strokes and penal servitude two years; the follower seventy-seven strokes and penal servitude one and a half years;
translations.idiomatic: Horse thieves on a first offense: the ringleader receives eighty-seven strokes and two years of penal servitude; the follower seventy-seven strokes and one and a half years;

sentences.zh: 再犯加等，罪止一百七，出軍。

translations.literal: on a repeat offense increase the degree; the penalty stops at one hundred seven strokes and banishment to military service.
translations.idiomatic: on repeat offense the penalty increases, up to one hundred seven strokes and banishment to military service.

sentences.zh: 盜牛者，初犯為首七十七，徒一年半，為從六十七，徒一年；

translations.literal: Those who steal cattle: on a first offense the ringleader receives seventy-seven strokes and penal servitude one and a half years; the follower sixty-seven strokes and penal servitude one year;
translations.idiomatic: Cattle thieves on a first offense: the ringleader receives seventy-seven strokes and one and a half years of penal servitude; the follower sixty-seven strokes and one year;

sentences.zh: 再犯加等，罪止一百七，出軍。

translations.literal: on a repeat offense increase the degree; the penalty stops at one hundred seven strokes and banishment to military service.
translations.idiomatic: on repeat offense the penalty increases, up to one hundred seven strokes and banishment to military service.

sentences.zh: 盜驢騾者，初犯為首六十七，徒一年，為從五十七，刺放；

translations.literal: Those who steal donkeys or mules: on a first offense the ringleader receives sixty-seven strokes and penal servitude one year; the follower fifty-seven strokes, tattoo, and release;
translations.idiomatic: Donkey or mule thieves on a first offense: the ringleader receives sixty-seven strokes and one year of penal servitude; the follower fifty-seven strokes, tattoo, and release;

sentences.zh: 再犯加等，罪止徒三年。

translations.literal: on a repeat offense increase the degree; the penalty stops at penal servitude three years.
translations.idiomatic: on repeat offense the penalty increases, up to three years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 盜羊豬者，初犯為首五十七，刺放，為從四十七，刺放；

translations.literal: Those who steal sheep or pigs: on a first offense the ringleader receives fifty-seven strokes, tattoo, and release; the follower forty-seven strokes, tattoo, and release;
translations.idiomatic: Sheep or pig thieves on a first offense: the ringleader receives fifty-seven strokes, tattoo, and release; the follower forty-seven strokes, tattoo, and release;

sentences.zh: 再犯加等，罪止徒三年。

translations.literal: on a repeat offense increase the degree; the penalty stops at penal servitude three years.
translations.idiomatic: on repeat offense the penalty increases, up to three years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 盜系官駝馬牛者，比常盜加一等。

translations.literal: As to all who steal official camels, horses, or cattle: one degree above ordinary theft.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of official camels, horses, or cattle is punished one degree above ordinary theft.

sentences.zh: 諸劇賊既款附得官，復以捕賊為由，虐取民財者，計贓論罪，流遠。

translations.literal: As to all notorious bandits who, having surrendered and received office, again extort the people's property under the pretext of catching thieves: sentence according to the loot and exile to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: Notorious bandits who, after surrendering and receiving office, extort the people under the pretext of catching thieves are sentenced according to the loot and exiled afar.

sentences.zh: 諸強盜再犯，仍刺。

translations.literal: As to all repeat offenders in robbery: still tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat robbers are still tattooed.

sentences.zh: 諸強盜殺傷事主，不分首從，皆處死。

translations.literal: As to all robbers who kill or injure the victim: without distinguishing ringleader and follower, all are executed.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers who kill or injure the victim are all executed, regardless of ringleader or follower.

sentences.zh: 諸強奪人財，以強盜論。

translations.literal: As to all who forcibly seize another's property: sentenced as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Those who forcibly seize another's property are sentenced as robbers.

sentences.zh: 諸以藥迷瞀人，取其財者，以強盜論。

translations.literal: As to all who drug people into stupor and take their property: sentenced as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Those who drug people into stupor and take their property are sentenced as robbers.

sentences.zh: 諸白晝持仗，剽掠得財，毆傷事主；

translations.literal: As to all who in broad daylight bear arms, plunder property, and beat and injure the victim;
translations.idiomatic: Those who in broad daylight bear arms, plunder property, and beat and injure the victim;

sentences.zh: 若得財，不曾傷事主，並以強盜論。

translations.literal: if property is obtained but the victim is not injured, all are sentenced as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: if property is obtained even without injuring the victim, all are sentenced as robbers.

sentences.zh: 諸官民行船，遭風著淺，輒有搶虜財物者，比同強盜科斷。

translations.literal: As to all officials and commoners traveling by boat who, when wind drives them aground, promptly plunder and seize property: sentenced the same as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners who plunder property when wind drives their boats aground are sentenced the same as robbers.

sentences.zh: 若會赦，仍不與真盜同論，征贓免罪。

translations.literal: If an amnesty is encountered, they are still not judged the same as true thieves; collect the loot and exempt the offense.
translations.idiomatic: If an amnesty applies, they are not treated like true thieves: the loot is collected and the offense exempted.

sentences.zh: 諸強盜出外國，其邊臣執以來獻者，賜金帛以旌之。

translations.literal: As to all robbers who flee abroad: if border officials capture and present them, gold and silk are bestowed to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers who flee abroad, when captured and presented by border officials, earn gold and silk rewards for their captors.

sentences.zh: 諸盜乘輿服御器物者，不分首從，皆處死。

translations.literal: As to all who steal the imperial carriage, regalia, or court utensils: without distinguishing ringleader and follower, all are executed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who steal the imperial carriage, regalia, or court utensils are all executed, regardless of ringleader or follower.

sentences.zh: 知情領賣，克除價錢者，減一等。

translations.literal: Those who knowingly receive and sell, deducting from the price: reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knowingly receive stolen goods for resale and deduct from the price receive one degree less punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸盜官錢，追征未盡，到官禁系既久，實無可折償者，除之。

translations.literal: As to all who steal official money: if pursuit of restitution is not complete, and after long imprisonment at court there is truly nothing with which to compensate, it is remitted.
translations.idiomatic: When stolen official money cannot be fully recovered and the offender, long imprisoned, truly has nothing left with which to compensate, the remainder is remitted.

sentences.zh: 諸守庫軍，但盜庫中財物者，處死，會赦者仍刺之。

translations.literal: As to all treasury guards who steal property from the treasury: execution; if an amnesty is encountered, still tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury guards who steal from the treasury are executed; if an amnesty applies, they are still tattooed.

sentences.zh: 諸內藏典守，輒盜庫中財物者，處死。

translations.literal: As to all inner-treasury keepers who steal property from the treasury: execution.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-treasury keepers who steal from the treasury are executed.

sentences.zh: 諸造鈔庫工匠，私藏合毀之鈔出庫者，杖一百七。

translations.literal: As to all note-printing craftsmen of the note treasury who privately hide notes marked for destruction and remove them from the treasury: beaten one hundred seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Note-printing craftsmen who hide notes marked for destruction and remove them from the treasury receive one hundred seven strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 監臨失關防者，笞三十七。

translations.literal: Supervisors who fail in guarding: thirty-seven strokes of the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors who fail in guarding receive thirty-seven strokes of the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 諸盜印鈔庫鈔者，處死。

translations.literal: As to all who steal newly printed notes from the note treasury: execution.
translations.idiomatic: Those who steal newly printed notes from the note treasury are executed.

sentences.zh: 諸檢昏鈔行人，盜取昏鈔，為監臨搜獲，不得財者，以盜庫藏錢物不得財加等論，杖七十七。

translations.literal: As to all worn-note inspectors who steal worn notes and are seized by their supervisor without obtaining property: sentenced one degree above theft from the treasury without obtaining property—beaten seventy-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Worn-note inspectors who steal worn notes and are seized by their supervisor without obtaining property are sentenced one degree above treasury theft without gain: seventy-seven strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 諸燒鈔庫合幹檢鈔行人，輒盜昏鈔出庫分使者，刺斷。

translations.literal: As to all worn-note inspectors attached to the note-burning treasury who steal worn notes from the treasury to distribute: tattoo and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Worn-note inspectors at the note-burning treasury who steal worn notes from the treasury to distribute them receive tattoo and banishment.

sentences.zh: 諸盜局院官物，雖贓不滿貫，仍加等，杖七十七，刺字。

translations.literal: As to all who steal government bureau property: even if the loot is under one guan, still increase the degree—beaten seventy-seven strokes and tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of government bureau property, even under one guan, still receives an increased penalty: seventy-seven strokes of the staff and tattooing.

sentences.zh: 諸工匠已關出庫物料，成造及額余外，不曾還官，因盜出局者，斷罪，免刺。

translations.literal: As to all craftsmen who, after materials have been issued from the storehouse, beyond what was made to quota and surplus, have not returned them to the state and steal them out of the bureau: sentenced, but exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen who, after materials were issued from the storehouse, keep surplus beyond quota and steal them from the bureau are sentenced but exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸盜已到倉官糧，而未離倉事覺者，以不得財論，免刺。

translations.literal: As to all who steal official grain already inside the granary but are discovered before leaving the granary: sentenced as for obtaining no property, exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Those who steal official grain inside the granary but are discovered before leaving it are sentenced as if no property was obtained and are exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸盜官員符節，比常盜加一等，計贓坐罪。

translations.literal: As to all who steal official seals and tallies: one degree above ordinary theft; sentence according to the value of the loot.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of official seals and tallies is punished one degree above ordinary theft, with sentence according to the value of the loot.

sentences.zh: 諸盜官府文卷作故紙變賣者，杖七十七，同竊盜，刺字；

translations.literal: As to all who steal government documents and sell them as scrap paper: beaten seventy-seven strokes, the same as petty theft, tattooed;
translations.idiomatic: Those who steal government documents and sell them as scrap paper receive seventy-seven strokes of the staff, the same as petty theft, and are tattooed;

sentences.zh: 買卷人笞四十七。

translations.literal: the buyer of the documents: forty-seven strokes of the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: the buyer of the documents receives forty-seven strokes of the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 諸圖財謀故殺人多者，淩遲處死，仍驗各賊所殺人數，於家屬均征燒埋銀。

translations.literal: As to all who plot for wealth and deliberately murder many people: executed by dismemberment; still verify the number each thief killed and levy burial compensation silver evenly from the families.
translations.idiomatic: Those who plot for wealth and deliberately murder many people suffer dismemberment; the number each killer slew is verified and burial compensation is levied evenly from their families.

sentences.zh: 諸圖財陷溺人於死，幸獲生免者，罪與已死同。

translations.literal: As to all who plot for wealth and trap someone in death but the victim fortunately survives: the offense is the same as if he had died.
translations.idiomatic: Those who plot for wealth and trap someone in mortal peril receive the same penalty as if the victim had died, even if he survives.

sentences.zh: 諸圖財殺死他人奴婢，即以圖財殺人論。

translations.literal: As to all who plot for wealth and kill another's slave or maid: sentenced as plotting for wealth and murder.
translations.idiomatic: Those who plot for wealth and kill another's slave or maid are sentenced for plotting wealth and murder.

sentences.zh: 諸奴盜主財而逃，送其逃者，輒殺其奴而取其財，即以強盜殺人論。

translations.literal: As to all cases where a slave steals the master's property and flees, and the one sent in pursuit kills the slave and takes the property: sentenced as robbery and murder.
translations.idiomatic: When a slave steals the master's property and flees, and the pursuer kills the slave and takes the property, the pursuer is sentenced for robbery and murder.

sentences.zh: 諸發冢，已開冢者同竊盜，開棺槨者同強盜，毀屍骸者同傷人，仍於犯人家屬征燒埋銀。

translations.literal: As to all grave opening: one who has opened the mound is treated the same as petty theft; one who has opened the coffin is treated the same as robbery; one who has destroyed the corpse is treated the same as injury; still levy burial compensation silver from the offender's family.
translations.idiomatic: Grave robbers who open the mound are treated as petty thieves; those who open the coffin as robbers; those who destroy the corpse as assailants; burial compensation is still levied from the offender's family.

sentences.zh: 諸挾仇發冢，盜棄其屍者，處死。

translations.literal: As to all who open graves bearing a grudge and discard the corpse: execution.
translations.idiomatic: Those who open graves out of enmity and discard the corpse are executed.

sentences.zh: 諸發冢得財不傷屍，杖一百七，刺配。

translations.literal: As to all who open graves, obtain property, and do not harm the corpse: beaten one hundred seven strokes, tattoo, and assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Grave robbers who obtain property without harming the corpse receive one hundred seven strokes of the staff, tattoo, and penal assignment.

sentences.zh: 諸盜發諸王駙馬墳寢者，不分首從，皆處死。

translations.literal: As to all who rob the tombs of princes and imperial sons-in-law: without distinguishing ringleader and follower, all are executed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rob the tombs of princes and imperial sons-in-law are all executed, regardless of ringleader or follower.

sentences.zh: 看守禁地人，杖一百七，三分家產，一分沒官，同看守人杖六十七。

translations.literal: The keeper of the forbidden ground: beaten one hundred seven strokes; one-third of household property confiscated, of which one part goes to the state; fellow keepers beaten sixty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The keeper of the forbidden ground receives one hundred seven strokes of the staff; one-third of his household property is confiscated, with one part going to the state; fellow keepers receive sixty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 諸事主殺死盜者，不坐。

translations.literal: As to all victims who kill a thief: no guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Victims who kill a thief are not guilty.

sentences.zh: 諸寅夜潛入人家，被毆傷而死者，勿論。

translations.literal: As to all who at night secretly enter a house and are beaten and killed: no prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: Those who enter a house secretly at night and are beaten and killed are not prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 諸於迥野盜伐人材木者，免刺，計贓科斷。

translations.literal: As to all who in remote wilds steal and cut another's timber: exempt from tattoo; sentence according to the value of the loot.
translations.idiomatic: Those who in remote wilds steal and cut another's timber are exempt from tattoo and sentenced according to the value of the loot.

sentences.zh: 諸被脅眾上盜，至盜所，復逃去，不以為從論。

translations.literal: As to all who are coerced in a crowd to join a robbery, reach the scene of theft, then flee: not treated as accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Those coerced in a crowd to join a robbery who reach the scene but then flee are not treated as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜贓不滿貫，斷罪，免刺。

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves whose loot is under one guan: sentenced, but exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves whose loot is under one guan are sentenced but exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸子為盜，父殺之，不坐。

translations.literal: As to all cases where a son is a thief and the father kills him: no guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When a son is a thief and the father kills him, the father is not guilty.

sentences.zh: 諸為盜，初經刺斷，再犯奸私，止以奸為坐，不以為盜再犯論。

translations.literal: As to all who, having once been tattooed and released for theft, again commit adultery: punished only for adultery, not counted as a repeat theft offense.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves once tattooed and released who later commit adultery are punished only for adultery, not as repeat thieves.

sentences.zh: 諸奴婢數為盜，應識過於門者，其主不知情，不得輒書於其主之門。

translations.literal: As to all slaves and maids who repeatedly steal and should have their offense marked at the door: if the master did not know, the mark must not be written on the master's door.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves and maids who repeatedly steal should have their offense marked at the door; if the master did not know, the mark must not be placed on the master's door.

sentences.zh: 諸被誘脅上盜，不曾分贓，而容隱不首者，杖六十七，免刺。

translations.literal: As to all who are enticed and coerced to join a robbery, receive no share of the loot, yet harbor the matter and do not report: beaten sixty-seven strokes, exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Those enticed and coerced to join a robbery who receive no share of the loot but harbor the matter without reporting receive sixty-seven strokes of the staff and are exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸先盜親屬財，免刺，再盜他人財，止作初犯論。

translations.literal: As to all who first steal a relative's property: exempt from tattoo; if they later steal another's property, count it only as a first offense.
translations.idiomatic: Those who first steal a relative's property are exempt from tattoo; if they later steal another's property, it is counted only as a first offense.

sentences.zh: 諸先犯誘奸婦人在逃，後犯竊盜，二事俱發，以誘奸為重，杖從奸，刺從盜。

translations.literal: As to all who first committed enticing adultery with a married woman and fled, then later committed petty theft: when both matters come to light together, enticing adultery is treated as the heavier offense—the staff beating follows the adultery statute, the tattoo follows the theft statute.
translations.idiomatic: Those who first seduced a married woman and fled, then later committed petty theft, are punished for both offenses together: adultery governs the staff beating, theft governs the tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸瘖啞為盜，不論瘖啞。

translations.literal: As to all mute and deaf persons who steal: their muteness and deafness are not considered.
translations.idiomatic: Mute and deaf thieves are punished without regard to disability.

sentences.zh: 諸詐稱搜稅，攔頭剽奪行李財物者，以盜論，刺斷，充警跡人。

translations.literal: As to all who falsely claim to be searching for taxes and waylay travelers to plunder luggage and property: sentenced as thieves, tattoo and banishment, assigned as police trackers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who feign a tax search to waylay travelers and plunder their goods are sentenced as thieves, tattooed and banished, and made police trackers.

sentences.zh: 諸盜米糧，非因饑饉者，仍刺斷。

translations.literal: As to all who steal grain and provisions when not driven by famine: still tattoo and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of grain not driven by famine still carries tattoo and banishment.

sentences.zh: 諸盜塔廟神像服飾，無人看守者，斷罪，免刺。

translations.literal: As to all who steal vestments of pagoda and temple images when no one guards them: sentenced, exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of unguarded temple image vestments brings conviction but no tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸事主及盜私相休和者，同罪；

translations.literal: As to all victims and thieves who privately settle with one another: both guilty;
translations.idiomatic: Victims and thieves who privately settle are both guilty;

sentences.zh: 所盜錢物頭匹、倍贓等，沒官。

translations.literal: stolen money, goods, livestock, double restitution, and the like are confiscated to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Stolen money, goods, livestock, and double restitution are confiscated to the state.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜應徒，若有祖父母、父母年老，無兼丁侍養者，刺斷免徒；

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves due for penal servitude: if grandparents or parents are elderly with no other son to support them, tattoo and banishment but exempt from servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves due for penal servitude who must support elderly grandparents or parents with no other son receive tattoo and banishment but are exempt from servitude.

sentences.zh: 再犯而親尚存者，候親終日，發遣居役。

translations.literal: If they reoffend while the relative still lives, wait until the relative dies, then send them to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Reoffenders wait until the dependent relative dies before serving their term.

sentences.zh: 諸女直人為盜，刺斷同漢人。

translations.literal: As to all Jurchen who steal: tattoo and banishment the same as Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen thieves receive the same tattoo and banishment as Han Chinese.

sentences.zh: 諸年饑民窮，見物而盜，計贓斷罪，免刺配及征倍贓。

translations.literal: As to all poor civilians in famine years who steal whatever they see: sentenced by value, exempt from tattoo, assignment, and double restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Poor civilians who steal in famine years are sentenced by value but exempt from tattoo, assignment, and double restitution.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜，一歲之中頻犯者，從一重，論刺斷。

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves who repeatedly offend within one year: apply the heavier offense with tattoo and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves who repeatedly offend within one year are sentenced on the heavier count with tattoo and banishment.

sentences.zh: 諸為盜為所得贓與人博不勝，失所得贓，事覺追正贓，仍坐博者罪。

translations.literal: As to all thieves who gamble away stolen goods and lose them: when discovered, recover the original goods; the gambler is still guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves who gamble away stolen goods must still make restitution when discovered, and the gambler remains guilty.

sentences.zh: 諸父以子同盜，子年未出幼，不曾分贓，免罪。

translations.literal: As to all fathers and sons who steal together when the son is still a minor and never shared loot: exempt from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When a father and minor son steal together and the son never shared loot, the son is exempt.

sentences.zh: 諸年饑，迫其子若婿同持仗行劫，子若婿減死一等，坐免刺，充警跡人。

translations.literal: As to all who in famine years force a son or son-in-law to join armed robbery: the son or son-in-law receives death reduced one degree, exempt from tattoo, assigned as police tracker.
translations.idiomatic: Sons or sons-in-law forced into famine-year armed robbery receive death reduced one degree, no tattoo, and assignment as police trackers.

sentences.zh: 諸父為人誘為盜，疾不能往，命其子從之，而分其贓者，父減為從一等，免刺，子以為從論。

translations.literal: As to all fathers enticed to steal who are too ill to go and send their sons to share loot: father reduced one degree as accomplice, exempt from tattoo; son sentenced as accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers too ill to steal who send sons to share loot are reduced one degree and exempt from tattoo; sons are accomplices.

sentences.zh: 諸兄逼未成丁弟同上盜，減為從一等論，仍罰贖。

translations.literal: As to all elder brothers who force underage younger brothers to steal: reduced one degree as accomplice, still fined in lieu.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brothers who force underage younger brothers to steal receive one degree less as accomplices and pay a fine in lieu.

sentences.zh: 諸兄弟同盜，罪皆至死，父母老而乏養者，內以一人情罪可逭者，免死養親。

translations.literal: As to all brothers who steal together when all face death and parents lack support: one whose circumstances allow may be spared death to support parents.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers who steal together and all face death may spare one member to support elderly parents.

sentences.zh: 諸兄弟同盜，皆刺。

translations.literal: As to all brothers who steal together: all are tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers who steal together are all tattooed.

sentences.zh: 諸父子兄弟頻同上盜，從凡盜首從論。

translations.literal: As to all fathers, sons, and brothers who repeatedly steal together: follow ordinary ringleader and accomplice rules.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers, sons, and brothers who repeatedly steal together follow ordinary ringleader-and-accomplice rules.

sentences.zh: 諸父子兄弟同為強盜者，皆處死。

translations.literal: As to all fathers, sons, and brothers who together commit robbery: all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers, sons, and brothers who commit robbery together are all executed.

sentences.zh: 諸夫謀為強盜，妻不諫，反從之盜者，減為從一等論罪。

translations.literal: As to all husbands who plot robbery and wives who join instead of dissuading: wife reduced one degree as accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Wives who join a husband's robbery instead of dissuading him are reduced one degree as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 諸親屬相盜，謂本服緦麻以上親，及大功以上共為婚姻之家，犯盜止坐其罪，並不在刺字、倍贓、再犯之限。

translations.literal: As to all theft among relatives within cap-and-sash mourning and affinal kin within great-merit mourning: only the offense itself is punished; tattoo, double restitution, and repeat rules do not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Theft among close natal and affinal kin is punished only for the offense itself, without tattoo, double restitution, or repeat-offense rules.

sentences.zh: 其別居尊長於卑幼家竊盜，若強盜及卑幼於尊長家行竊盜者，緦麻小功減凡人一等，大功減二等，期親減三等，強盜者準凡盜論，殺傷者各依故殺傷法。

translations.literal: When seniors in separate residence steal from juniors' households or juniors steal from seniors': cap-and-sash and small-merit kin reduced one degree, great-merit two degrees, close kin three degrees; robbery follows ordinary theft; killing and injury follow intentional homicide and injury statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Inter-household theft among kin is reduced one to three degrees by mourning grade; robbery follows ordinary theft; killing or injury follows homicide and assault statutes.

sentences.zh: 若同居卑幼將人盜己家財物者，五十貫以下，笞二十七，每五十貫加一等，罪止五十七，他人依常盜減一等。

translations.literal: If a co-resident junior brings outsiders to steal from his household: fifty strings or less, twenty-seven strokes; each fifty strings adds one degree up to fifty-seven; outsiders reduced one degree below ordinary theft.
translations.idiomatic: Co-resident juniors who bring outsiders to steal from their household receive twenty-seven strokes for fifty strings or less, increasing up to fifty-seven; outsiders are reduced one degree.

sentences.zh: 諸姑表侄盜姑夫財，同親屬相盜論。

translations.literal: As to all paternal aunt's nephews who steal from the aunt's husband: judged as theft among relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Paternal aunt's nephews who steal from the uncle are judged as theft among relatives.

sentences.zh: 諸女在室，喪其父，不能自存，有祖父母而不之恤，因盜祖父母錢者，不坐。

translations.literal: As to all unmarried daughters orphaned and neglected by grandparents who steal from them: not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned daughters neglected by grandparents who steal from them are not guilty.

sentences.zh: 諸弟為首強劫從兄財，即以強盜論。

translations.literal: As to all younger brothers who lead forcible robbery against elder male cousins: sentenced as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers who forcibly rob elder male cousins are sentenced as robbers.

sentences.zh: 諸嘗過房他人子孫以為子孫，輒盜所過房之家財物者，即以親屬相盜論。

translations.literal: As to all who adopt another's descendants and steal from the adopting household: judged as theft among relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Those who adopt descendants and then steal from the adopting household are judged as theft among relatives.

sentences.zh: 諸奴盜主財，應流遠，而主求免者聽。

translations.literal: As to all slaves who steal their master's property and are due for distant exile: if the master requests exemption, permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves due for exile for stealing from masters may be exempted at the master's request.

sentences.zh: 諸奴盜主財，斷罪，免刺。

translations.literal: As to all slaves who steal their master's property: sentenced, exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves who steal from masters are sentenced but exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸盜雇主財者，免刺，不追倍贓。

translations.literal: As to all who steal from a current employer: exempt from tattoo and double restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Theft from a current employer is exempt from tattoo and double restitution.

sentences.zh: 盜先雇主財者，同常盜論。

translations.literal: Those who steal from a former employer: judged as ordinary theft.
translations.idiomatic: Theft from a former employer is ordinary theft.

sentences.zh: 諸佃客盜地主財，同常盜論。

translations.literal: As to all tenant farmers who steal from landlords: judged as ordinary theft.
translations.idiomatic: Tenant farmers who steal from landlords are ordinary thieves.

sentences.zh: 諸同主奴相盜，斷罪，免刺配，不追倍贓。

translations.literal: As to all slaves under the same master who steal from one another: sentenced, exempt from tattoo and assignment, no double restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves of the same master who steal from one another are sentenced but exempt from tattoo, assignment, and double restitution.

sentences.zh: 諸盜同受雇人財，不以同居論。

translations.literal: As to all who steal from fellow employees: not treated as co-residence.
translations.idiomatic: Theft from fellow employees is not co-residence theft.

sentences.zh: 諸賃屋與房主同居，而盜房主財者，與常盜論。

translations.literal: As to all who rent and co-reside with a landlord but steal the landlord's property: judged as ordinary theft.
translations.idiomatic: Tenants who co-reside with landlords but steal from them are ordinary thieves.

sentences.zh: 諸盜同本財者，笞五十七，不以真盜計贓論。

translations.literal: As to all who steal shared capital: fifty-seven strokes of the bamboo, not valued as true theft.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of shared capital brings fifty-seven strokes and is not valued as true theft.

sentences.zh: 諸巡捕軍兵因自為盜者，比常盜加一等論罪；

translations.literal: As to all patrol soldiers who themselves steal: sentenced one degree above ordinary theft;
translations.idiomatic: Patrol soldiers who steal are sentenced one degree above ordinary theft;

sentences.zh: 若自相覺察，告捕到官，或曾共為盜，首獲同伴者，免罪給賞。

translations.literal: if they expose one another, report and capture offenders, or having stolen together are first to capture a companion: exempt and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: If they expose one another, deliver offenders, or first capture a former accomplice, they are exempt and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 諸軍人為盜，刺斷，免充警跡人，仍追賞錢給告者。

translations.literal: As to all soldiers who steal: tattoo and banishment, exempt from police-tracker assignment, reward still paid to informant.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who steal are tattooed and banished, exempt from police-tracker duty, with reward still paid to informants.

sentences.zh: 諸守庫藏軍人，輒為首誘引外人偷盜官物，但經二次三次入庫為盜，又提鈴把門軍人，受贓縱賊者，皆處死。

translations.literal: As to all treasury guards who lead outsiders to steal official goods repeatedly, and gate guards who take bribes and release thieves: all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury guards who lead repeated thefts and gate guards who take bribes to release thieves are all executed.

sentences.zh: 為從者杖一百七，刺字流遠。

translations.literal: Accomplices: one hundred seven strokes, tattoo, distant exile.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplices receive one hundred seven strokes, tattoo, and distant exile.

sentences.zh: 諸見役軍人在逃，因為竊盜得財，杖一百七，仍刺字，杖從逃軍，刺從盜。

translations.literal: As to all active deserters who commit petty theft for gain: one hundred seven strokes and tattooed—staff from deserter statute, tattoo from theft statute.
translations.idiomatic: Active deserters who steal receive one hundred seven strokes and tattoo under the deserter and theft statutes respectively.

sentences.zh: 諸軍人在路奪人財物，又迫逐人致死非命者，為首杖一百七，為從七十七，征燒埋銀給苦主。

translations.literal: As to all soldiers who seize property on the road and in pursuit cause accidental death: ringleader one hundred seven strokes, accomplice seventy-seven, burial silver for victim's family.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who seize property on the road and cause death in pursuit receive one hundred seven or seventy-seven strokes, with burial compensation for the family.

sentences.zh: 諸婦人為盜，斷罪，免刺配及充警跡人，免征倍贓，再犯並坐其夫。

translations.literal: As to all women who steal: sentenced, exempt from tattoo, assignment, and police-tracker duty, exempt from double restitution; on reoffense the husband is punished too.
translations.idiomatic: Women who steal are sentenced but exempt from tattoo, assignment, police-tracker duty, and double restitution; on reoffense the husband is punished too.

sentences.zh: 諸婦人寡居與人奸，盜舅姑財與奸夫，令娶己為妻者，奸非奸所捕獲，止以同居卑幼盜尊長財為坐，笞五十七，歸宗，奸夫杖六十七。

translations.literal: As to all widows who commit adultery, steal from in-laws for a lover, and have him marry them: if not caught in adultery, punished as co-resident junior stealing from senior—fifty-seven strokes, return to clan; lover sixty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Widows who steal from in-laws for lovers and marry them—if adultery was not caught—are punished as juniors stealing from seniors: fifty-seven strokes and return to clan; lovers receive sixty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 諸偽僧竊取佛像腹中裝者，以盜論。

translations.literal: As to all false monks who steal contents from inside Buddha images: sentenced as thieves.
translations.idiomatic: False monks who steal from inside Buddha statues are sentenced as thieves.

sentences.zh: 諸僧道為盜，同常盜，刺斷，征倍贓，還俗充警跡人。

translations.literal: As to all monks and Daoist priests who steal: same as ordinary thieves, tattoo and banishment, double restitution, laicization, police-tracker assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Daoists who steal are punished like ordinary thieves, with tattoo, banishment, double restitution, laicization, and police-tracker assignment.

sentences.zh: 諸僧道盜其親師祖、師父及同師兄弟財者，免刺，不追倍贓，斷罪還俗。

translations.literal: As to all monks and Daoists who steal from lineage grandmaster, teacher, or fellow disciples: exempt from tattoo and double restitution, sentenced and laicized.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Daoists who steal from teachers or fellow disciples are exempt from tattoo and double restitution but are sentenced and laicized.

sentences.zh: 諸幼小為盜，事發長大，以幼小論。

translations.literal: As to all who steal while young and the matter comes to light after they have grown: judged as minors.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stole as minors but are discovered after reaching adulthood are judged as minors.

sentences.zh: 未老疾為盜，事發老疾，以老疾論。

translations.literal: Those who steal before old age or infirmity and are discovered after becoming old or infirm: judged as old or infirm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stole while still hale but are discovered after becoming elderly or infirm are judged accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其所當罪，聽贖，仍免刺配，諸犯罪亦如之。

translations.literal: For the penalty they would receive, ransom is permitted, and tattoo and penal assignment are still waived; other crimes follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: They may ransom the penalty and are exempt from tattoo and penal assignment; the same rule applies to other crimes.

sentences.zh: 諸年未出幼，再犯竊盜者，仍免刺贖罪，發充警跡人。

translations.literal: As to all who have not yet reached majority and reoffend in petty theft: still exempt from tattoo and may ransom the offense, assigned as police trackers.
translations.idiomatic: Minors who reoffend in petty theft may still ransom the offense without tattoo and are assigned as police trackers.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜年幼者為首，年長者為從，為首仍聽贖免刺配，為從依常律。

translations.literal: As to all petty thefts where the younger is ringleader and the older accomplice: the ringleader may still ransom and is exempt from tattoo and assignment; the accomplice follows the ordinary statute.
translations.idiomatic: When the younger thief is ringleader and the older accomplice, the ringleader may ransom and avoid tattoo and assignment; the accomplice follows ordinary rules.

sentences.zh: 諸掏摸人身上錢物者，初犯、再犯、三犯，刺斷徒流，並同竊盜法，仍以赦後為坐。

translations.literal: As to all pickpockets: first, second, and third offenses—tattoo, banishment, servitude, and exile all follow the petty-theft statute, reckoned from after amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Pickpockets receive tattoo, banishment, servitude, or exile under the petty-theft rules for first through third offenses, counted from after any amnesty.

sentences.zh: 諸以七十二局欺誘良家子弟、富商大賈，博塞錢物者，以竊盜論，計贓斷配。

translations.literal: As to all who use seventy-two gambling schemes to deceive respectable youths and wealthy merchants: sentenced as petty thieves, exile by value of loot.
translations.idiomatic: Those who use rigged gambling schemes to swindle respectable youths and wealthy merchants are sentenced as petty thieves with exile by value.

sentences.zh: 諸夜發同舟橐中裝，取其財者，與竊盜真犯同論。

translations.literal: As to all who at night open fellow travelers' luggage on the same boat and take property: judged as true petty thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who at night open fellow passengers' luggage on the same boat and steal property are punished as convicted petty thieves.

sentences.zh: 諸略賣良人為奴婢者，略賣一人，杖一百七，流遠；

translations.literal: As to all who abduct and sell free persons as slaves: for one person, one hundred seven strokes and distant exile;
translations.idiomatic: Abducting and selling one free person as a slave brings one hundred seven strokes and exile;

sentences.zh: 二人以上，處死；

translations.literal: for two or more: execution.
translations.idiomatic: for two or more victims: execution.

sentences.zh: 為妻妾子孫者，一百七，徒三年；

translations.literal: if made wives, concubines, or descendants: one hundred seven strokes, three years penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Making them wives, concubines, or descendants brings one hundred seven strokes and three years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 因而殺傷人者，同強盜法。

translations.literal: if killing or injury results: the same as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone is killed or injured, the offense is treated as robbery.

sentences.zh: 若略而未賣者，減一等，和誘者又各減一等，及和同相賣為奴婢者，各一百七。

translations.literal: if abducted but not sold: reduce one degree; coaxers each reduced one degree further; those who mutually sell one another as slaves: each one hundred seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Abduction without sale reduces the penalty one degree; coaxing one degree further; mutual sale into slavery brings one hundred seven strokes each.

sentences.zh: 略誘奴婢，貨賣為奴婢者，各減誘略良人罪一等；

translations.literal: Those who abduct or coax slaves and sell them as slaves: each one degree less than for free persons.
translations.idiomatic: Abducting or coaxing slaves for sale brings penalties one degree lighter than for free persons.

sentences.zh: 為妻妾子孫者，七十七，徒一年半；

translations.literal: if made wives, concubines, or descendants: seventy-seven strokes, one and a half years penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Making abducted slaves wives, concubines, or descendants brings seventy-seven strokes and one and a half years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 知情娶買及藏匿受錢者，各遞減犯人罪一等。

translations.literal: Those who knowingly marry or buy, or harbor and receive money: each one degree less than the offender in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing buyers, marryers, or harborers each receive one degree less than the offender in sequence.

sentences.zh: 假以過房乞養為名，因而貨賣為奴婢者，九十七，引領牙保知情，減二等，價沒官，人給親。

translations.literal: Selling as slaves under pretense of adoption or foster care: ninety-seven strokes; knowing brokers reduced two degrees; price confiscated; person returned to kin.
translations.idiomatic: Selling persons as slaves under false adoption pretenses brings ninety-seven strokes; knowing brokers are reduced two degrees; the price is confiscated and the victim returned to kin.

sentences.zh: 如無元買契券，有司輒給公據者，及承告不即追捕者，並笞四十七。

translations.literal: If there is no original purchase contract and officials issue public certificates, or if upon report they do not immediately pursue: all forty-seven strokes of the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who issue certificates without purchase contracts or fail to pursue immediately upon report all receive forty-seven strokes of the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 關津主司知而受財縱放者，減犯人罪三等，除名不敘，失檢察者笞二十七。

translations.literal: Checkpoint officials who knowingly take bribes and release offenders: three degrees less than the offender, dismissed without reinstatement; those who fail to inspect: twenty-seven strokes of the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Checkpoint officials who take bribes to release offenders are punished three degrees below the offender and permanently dismissed; failed inspection brings twenty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 如能告獲者，略人每人給賞三十貫，和誘每人二十貫，以至元鈔為則，於犯人名下追征，無財者征及知情安主，牙保應捕人減半。

translations.literal: If they report and capture: thirty strings per abducted person, twenty per coaxed person in Zhiyuan notes, collected from the offender or knowing harborers; brokers and catchers receive half.
translations.idiomatic: Informants receive thirty strings per abducted person and twenty per coaxed person in Zhiyuan notes, collected from the offender or knowing harborers; brokers and catchers receive half.

sentences.zh: 其事未發而自首者，若同黨能悔過自首，擒獲其徒黨者，並原其罪，仍給賞之半。

translations.literal: If undiscovered and they surrender, or accomplices repent, surrender, and capture fellows: all pardoned and still receive half the reward.
translations.idiomatic: Voluntary surrender before discovery, or accomplices who repent and capture co-conspirators, are pardoned and still receive half the reward.

sentences.zh: 再犯及因略傷人者，不在首原之例。

translations.literal: Repeat offenders and those who injure through abduction are not within self-surrender pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat offenders and those who injure during abduction are not eligible for surrender pardon.

sentences.zh: 諸婦人誘賣良人，罪應徒者，免徒。

translations.literal: As to all women who abduct and sell free persons: if penal servitude would apply, servitude is waived.
translations.idiomatic: Women who abduct and sell free persons are exempt from penal servitude when it would otherwise apply.

sentences.zh: 諸職官誘略良人為奴，革後不首，仍除名不敘，所誘略人給親。

translations.literal: As to all officials who abduct free persons as slaves: after dismissal, if they do not surrender, still permanently dismissed; abducted persons returned to kin.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who abduct free persons as slaves and fail to surrender after dismissal are permanently struck from the rolls; victims are returned to kin.

sentences.zh: 諸兄盜牛，脅其弟同宰殺者，弟不坐。

translations.literal: As to all cases where an elder brother steals an ox and coerces his younger brother to slaughter it: the younger brother is not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: When an elder brother steals an ox and coerces a younger brother to help slaughter it, the younger brother is not guilty.

sentences.zh: 諸白晝剽奪驛馬，為首者處死，為從減一等流遠。

translations.literal: As to all who seize relay horses in broad daylight: ringleader executed; accomplice one degree less and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing relay horses in broad daylight brings execution for the ringleader and one degree less plus exile for accomplices.

sentences.zh: 諸盜親屬馬牛，事未覺自首，願償價，不從，既送官，仍以自首論免刺。

translations.literal: As to all who steal relatives' horses or cattle: if before discovery they surrender and offer compensation refused, then sent to court, still treated as surrender and exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives who steal horses or cattle and surrender with refused compensation before trial are still treated as voluntary surrender and exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸強盜行劫，為主所逐，分散奔走，為首者殺傷鄰人，為從者不知，不以殺傷事主不分首從論，為首者處死，為從者杖一百七，刺配。

translations.literal: As to all robbers pursued by the victim who scatter: if the ringleader kills or injures a neighbor while accomplices did not know, do not apply the rule on injuring the owner without distinguishing roles; ringleader executed, accomplice one hundred seven strokes, tattoo and assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing robbers whose ringleader kills a bystander unknown to accomplices are not judged by the owner-injury rule without distinction: the ringleader is executed; accomplices receive one hundred seven strokes, tattoo, and assignment.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜棄財拒捕，毆傷事主者，杖一百七，免刺。

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves who abandon loot, resist arrest, and beat the victim: one hundred seven strokes, exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves who abandon loot, resist arrest, and beat the victim receive one hundred seven strokes but are exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸為盜先竊後強，會赦，其下手殺傷事主者，不赦，余仍刺而釋之。

translations.literal: As to all who first steal then rob and encounter amnesty: subordinates who kill or injure the owner are not amnestied; the rest are tattooed and released.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves who escalate to robbery under amnesty: subordinates who kill or injure the owner are not pardoned; others are tattooed and released.

sentences.zh: 諸盜賊分贓不均，從賊欲首，為首賊所殺者，仍以謀故殺人論。

translations.literal: As to all bandits who divide loot unequally and whose ringleader kills an accomplice who wished to confess: still sentenced for intentional homicide.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits who kill an accomplice who wished to confess over unequal loot division are still sentenced for intentional homicide.

sentences.zh: 諸盜賊聞赦，故殺捕盜之人者，不赦。

translations.literal: As to all bandits who upon hearing of amnesty deliberately kill thief-catchers: not amnestied.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits who kill thief-catchers upon hearing of an amnesty are not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 諸藏匿強竊盜賊，有主謀糾合，指引上盜，分受贓物者，身雖不行，合以為首論。

translations.literal: As to all who harbor robbers or thieves when a mastermind organizes, directs the raid, and shares loot: though not present in person, sentenced as ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Harborers when a mastermind organizes, directs, and shares loot are sentenced as ringleaders even if not present.

sentences.zh: 若未行盜，及行盜之後，知情藏匿之家，各減強竊從賊一等科斷，免刺，其已經斷，怙終不改者，與從賊同。

translations.literal: If robbery not yet committed, or after committed, knowing harbor households: each one degree less than accomplice robbers or thieves, exempt from tattoo; if already sentenced and unrepentant, treated as accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing harborers before or after robbery receive one degree less than accomplices and are exempt from tattoo; persistent harborers after sentencing are treated as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 諸謀欲圖人所質之田，輒遣人強劫贖田之價者，主謀、下手一體刺斷，其卑幼為尊長驅役者免刺。

translations.literal: As to all who plot to seize pledged fields and send men to forcibly seize redemption payments: mastermind and executors alike tattooed and banished; juniors compelled by seniors exempt from tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Those who scheme to seize pledged land and extort redemption payments are tattooed and banished alike; juniors compelled by seniors are exempt from tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸盜賊應徵正贓及燒埋銀，貧無以備，令其折庸。

translations.literal: As to all thieves who owe original restitution and burial silver but are too poor: ordered to labor in lieu.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves too poor to pay restitution and burial compensation must work off the debt.

sentences.zh: 凡折庸，視各處庸價而會之。

translations.literal: For all labor in lieu of payment, reckon according to local wage rates.
translations.idiomatic: Labor in lieu of payment is reckoned by local wage rates.

sentences.zh: 庸滿發元籍，充警跡人。

translations.literal: When labor is complete, return to original register and assign as police trackers.
translations.idiomatic: When labor ends, offenders return to their register and are assigned as police trackers.

sentences.zh: 婦人日準男子工價三分之二，官錢役於旁近之處，私錢役於事主之家。

translations.literal: Women's daily wage is two-thirds of men's; government debts worked nearby, private debts at the victim's household.
translations.idiomatic: Women's daily wage is two-thirds of men's; public debts are worked nearby, private debts at the victim's home.

sentences.zh: 諸盜賊得財，用於酒肆倡優之家，不知情，止於本盜追征。

translations.literal: As to all stolen goods spent at taverns or brothels without proprietors' knowledge: recovery only from the thief.
translations.idiomatic: Stolen goods spent at taverns or brothels without the proprietors' knowledge are recovered only from the thief.

sentences.zh: 其所盜即官錢，雖不知情，於所用之家追征。

translations.literal: If the stolen goods were government money, even without knowledge, recovery is pursued from the spending household.
translations.idiomatic: If stolen government money was spent, recovery is pursued from the household even without knowledge.

sentences.zh: 若用買貨物，還其貨物，征元贓。

translations.literal: If used to buy goods, return the goods and collect the original stolen value.
translations.idiomatic: If stolen money bought goods, the goods are returned and the original value collected.

sentences.zh: 諸奴婢盜人牛馬，既斷罪，其贓無可征者，以其人給物主，其主願贖者聽。

translations.literal: As to all slaves who steal cattle or horses: once sentenced, if loot cannot be recovered, the person is given to the owner; the master may redeem if he wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves who steal cattle or horses, if restitution cannot be made, are given to the owner; the master may redeem them.

sentences.zh: 諸盜官錢，追征未盡，到官禁系既久，實無可折償者，除之。

translations.literal: As to all who steal official money: if recovery is incomplete and after long imprisonment there is truly nothing to compensate, remitted.
translations.idiomatic: When stolen official money cannot be recovered and the long-imprisoned offender has nothing left, the remainder is remitted.

sentences.zh: 諸系官人口盜人牛馬，免征倍贓。

translations.literal: As to all government-bound persons who steal cattle or horses: exempt from double restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Government-bound persons who steal cattle or horses are exempt from double restitution.

sentences.zh: 諸盜賊正贓已征給主，倍贓無可追理者，免征。

translations.literal: As to all thieves whose original restitution was paid to the owner but double restitution cannot be recovered: waived.
translations.idiomatic: When original restitution was paid but double restitution cannot be recovered, the double portion is waived.

sentences.zh: 諸盜賊正贓，或曲質於人，典主不知情，而歸其贓，仍征還元價。

translations.literal: As to all original stolen goods secretly pawned: if the pawnbroker did not know and returns them, the original price is still collected.
translations.idiomatic: If stolen goods were pawned without the pawnbroker's knowledge and returned, the original price is still collected.

sentences.zh: 諸遐荒盜賊，盜駝馬牛驢羊，倍贓無可征者，就發配役出軍。

translations.literal: As to all frontier thieves who steal livestock and cannot pay double restitution: assigned to penal service or military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier thieves who steal livestock and cannot pay double restitution are sent to penal service or the army.

sentences.zh: 諸盜先犯後發，與後犯先發罪同者，勿論。

translations.literal: As to all cases where an earlier offense is discovered later and a later offense earlier but the crimes are the same: no distinction.
translations.idiomatic: When discovery order would not change the penalty, no distinction is made.

sentences.zh: 諸先犯強盜刺斷，再犯竊盜，止依再犯竊盜刺配。

translations.literal: As to all first tattooed and banished for robbery who reoffend in petty theft: sentenced only for repeat petty theft with tattoo and assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Those first tattooed for robbery who later commit petty theft are sentenced only for repeat petty theft with tattoo and assignment.

sentences.zh: 諸出軍賊徒在逃，初犯杖六十七，再犯加二等，罪止一百七，仍發元流所出軍。

translations.literal: As to all military exiles who are bandits at large: first offense sixty-seven strokes of the staff; repeat offense increase two degrees, penalty stops at one hundred seven strokes, still dispatched to military service at the original place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Military exiles who are bandits at large receive sixty-seven strokes on the first offense and two degrees more on repeat, up to one hundred seven strokes, and are still sent to military service at their original exile post.

sentences.zh: 諸強竊盜充警跡人者，五年不犯，除其籍。

translations.literal: As to all robbers and thieves assigned as police trackers: if they do not offend for five years, remove them from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers and thieves assigned as police trackers are removed from the register after five years without offense.

sentences.zh: 其能告發，及捕獲強盜一名，減二年，二名比五年，竊盜一名減一半，應除籍之外，所獲多者，依常人獲盜理賞，不及數者，給憑通理。

translations.literal: If they can report or capture one robber, reduce two years; two robbers count as five years; one petty thief counts as half; beyond registry removal, if they capture more, reward follows ordinary thief-catching rules; if the number falls short, issue credentials to carry forward.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting or capturing one robber reduces the term by two years; two robbers count as five years; one petty thief as half; beyond registry removal, extra captures earn ordinary rewards, or credentials if the quota is not met.

sentences.zh: 籍既除，再犯，終身拘籍之。

translations.literal: Once the register is removed, on reoffense they are registered for life.
translations.idiomatic: After registry removal, a new offense leads to lifetime registration.

sentences.zh: 凡警跡人緝捕之外，有司毋差遣出入，妨其理生。

translations.literal: Apart from pursuit and capture, officials must not dispatch police trackers on errands that interfere with their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond pursuit duties, officials must not send police trackers on errands that disrupt their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 諸警跡人，有不告知鄰佑輒離家經宿，及遊惰不事生產作業者，有司究之，鄰佑有失覺察者，亦罪之。

translations.literal: As to all police trackers who leave home overnight without informing neighbors, or who are idle and do not engage in productive work: officials shall investigate; neighbors who fail to notice are also punished.
translations.idiomatic: Police trackers who stay out overnight without telling neighbors, or who are idle and unproductive, are investigated; neighbors who fail to notice are punished too.

sentences.zh: 諸警跡人受命捕盜，既獲其盜，卻挾恨殺其盜而取其財，不以平人殺有罪賊人論。

translations.literal: As to all police trackers who, having captured a thief, kill him in a grudge and take his property: not sentenced as a civilian killing a guilty thief.
translations.idiomatic: Police trackers who kill a captured thief out of spite and take his property are not treated as civilians killing guilty thieves.

sentences.zh: 諸色目人犯盜，免刺科斷，發本管官司設法拘檢，限內改過者，除其籍。

translations.literal: As to all Semuren who steal: exempt from tattoo and sentencing, sent to their supervising office for regulated detention; if they reform within the time limit, remove them from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Semuren thieves are exempt from tattooing and ordinary sentencing and are detained by their supervising office; reform within the limit removes them from the register.

sentences.zh: 無本管官司發付者，從有司收充警跡人。

translations.literal: If there is no supervising office to send them to, the authorities shall take them as police trackers.
translations.idiomatic: If no supervising office exists, the authorities assign them as police trackers.

sentences.zh: 諸為盜經刺，自除其字，再犯非理者，補刺。

translations.literal: As to all thieves who were tattooed and erase the characters themselves: on unreasonable reoffense, tattoo again.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooed thieves who erase their marks and reoffend unreasonably are tattooed again.

sentences.zh: 五年不再犯，已除籍者，不補刺，年未滿者仍補刺。

translations.literal: If they do not reoffend for five years and the register is already removed, do not re-tattoo; if the five years are not complete, still re-tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: After five years without offense with registry already removed, no re-tattooing; if five years are incomplete, re-tattooing still applies.

sentences.zh: 諸盜賊赦前擅去所刺字，不再犯，赦後不補刺。

translations.literal: As to all thieves who before an amnesty remove their tattoos without reoffending: after the amnesty, do not re-tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves who remove tattoos before an amnesty without reoffending are not re-tattooed after the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 諸應刺左右臂，而臂有雕青者，隨上下空歇之處刺之。

translations.literal: As to all who should be tattooed on left and right arms but have decorative blue tattoos: tattoo in vacant spaces above or below.
translations.idiomatic: Those due for arm tattoos who already have decorative blue tattoos are marked in vacant spaces above or below.

sentences.zh: 諸犯竊盜已經刺臂，卻遍文其身，覆蓋元刺，再犯竊盜，於手背刺之。

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves already tattooed on the arm who then tattoo the whole body to cover the original mark: on repeat petty theft, tattoo the back of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves who cover an arm tattoo with full-body designs are tattooed on the hand on repeat offense.

sentences.zh: 諸累犯竊盜，左右項臂刺遍，而再犯者，於項上空處刺之。

translations.literal: As to all repeat petty thieves tattooed on left, right, neck, and arms who offend again: tattoo on a vacant place on the neck.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat petty thieves already tattooed on arms and neck receive the next mark on a vacant spot on the neck.

sentences.zh: 諸子盜父首、弟盜兄首、婿盜翁首，並同自首者免罪。

translations.literal: As to all sons who steal and surrender their fathers' heads, younger brothers who steal and surrender elder brothers' heads, and sons-in-law who steal and surrender fathers-in-law's heads: all are exempt like voluntary surrenderants.
translations.idiomatic: Sons, younger brothers, or sons-in-law who steal and surrender a father's, elder brother's, or father-in-law's head are exempt as if they had surrendered voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 諸奴盜主首者，斷罪免刺，不征倍贓，仍付其主為奴。

translations.literal: As to all slaves who steal and surrender their master's head: sentenced, exempt from tattoo, no double restitution, still returned to the master as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves who steal and surrender their master's head are sentenced without tattoo or double restitution and remain their master's slaves.

sentences.zh: 諸脅從上盜，而不受贓者，止以不首之罪罪之，杖六十七，不刺。

translations.literal: As to all coerced to join a robbery but receive no loot: punished only for failure to report, sixty-seven strokes, no tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Those coerced into robbery without receiving loot are punished only for failing to report, with sixty-seven strokes and no tattoo.

sentences.zh: 諸為盜悔過，以所盜贓還主者免罪。

translations.literal: As to all thieves who repent and return stolen goods to the owner: exempt from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves who repent and return stolen goods to the owner are exempt from guilt.

sentences.zh: 諸為盜得財者，聞有涉疑根捕，卻以贓還主者，減二等論罪，免徒刺及倍贓。

translations.literal: As to all thieves who obtained property and, hearing of suspicion and pursuit, return the loot to the owner: reduce two degrees, exempt from servitude, tattoo, and double restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves who return loot upon hearing of pursuit have the penalty reduced two degrees and are exempt from servitude, tattoo, and double restitution.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜因事主盤詰，而自首服，其贓未還主者，計贓減二等論罪，刺字。

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves who confess when questioned by the victim while loot is not yet returned: sentence by value reduced two degrees, tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves who confess when the victim questions them before loot is returned are sentenced two degrees lower by value and tattooed.

sentences.zh: 諸盜贓，為首者自首，免罪，為從不首仍全科。

translations.literal: As to all stolen goods where the ringleader surrenders: exempt from guilt; accomplices who do not surrender still receive full penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the ringleader surrenders, he is exempt; accomplices who do not surrender receive the full penalty.

sentences.zh: 諸無服之親，相首為盜，止科其罪，免刺配倍贓。

translations.literal: As to all distantly related kin who report one another for theft: punish only the offense, exempt from tattoo, assignment, and double restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Distant kin who report one another for theft are punished for the offense only, without tattoo, assignment, or double restitution.

sentences.zh: 諸竊盜悔過，以贓還主不盡，其餘贓猶及刺罪者，仍刺之。

translations.literal: As to all petty thieves who repent and return loot incompletely: if the remainder still warrants tattoo, still tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves who repent but return loot incompletely are still tattooed if the remainder warrants it.
